info.title: PayPetal Merchant API
info.description:
The PayPetal Merchant API lets you accept payments, manage customers, and hold funds in escrow through a single REST interface.

**Authentication:** All protected endpoints require a JWT Bearer token obtained from `POST /api/auth/login`. Tokens are valid for 7 days.

**Base64 credential format:** `base64(secretKey:appId)`

**Two escrow products:**
- **TrustCore** — merchant-controlled escrow: you decide when to release or refund funds.
- **TrustVault** — customer-controlled escrow: funds release when the customer supplies a one-time code.

tags.name: TrustVault Escrow
tags.description:
TrustVault is a **customer-controlled** escrow product. Unlike TrustCore, the merchant does not trigger the release — the customer does.

**Typical flow:**
1. Call `POST /agreement` to create an agreement — you receive a hosted payment URL.
2. Redirect the customer to the payment URL to fund the escrow.
3. When the customer is satisfied and ready to release funds, call `PUT /agreement/auth/{reference}` to send them a one-time code by email.
4. The customer supplies the code to `PUT /agreement/complete/{reference}` to release the funds to the merchant.

This flow is suited for situations where the buyer controls the release — freelance work, service delivery, peer-to-peer sales.

tags.name: Payments
tags.description: Generate hosted payment links and verify transaction status. The customer is redirected to a PayPetal-hosted page to complete payment from their wallet. **Rate limit:** 60 requests per 60-second window per merchant on POST /pay/initiate.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: Manage the end-users registered under your merchant account. A customer record is required before you can add them to a TrustCore escrow agreement as either the payer or receiver. The `customerId` returned on creation is the stable identifier used across all escrow operations.

tags.name: TrustCore Payout Accounts
tags.description:
Manage the bank payout accounts used for TrustCore escrow releases and refunds.

**Why this is required:** before you can call `PUT /trustcore/{reference}/complete` or `PUT /trustcore/{reference}/refund`, the destination customer must have a verified bank account on file.

**Recommended flow:**
1. Call `GET /api/v1/account/banks` to retrieve the list of supported banks and their codes.
2. Call `POST /api/v1/account/bank/validate` to resolve the account number to an account name — confirm this with the customer.
3. Call `POST /api/v1/escrow/trustcore/payout/{customerId}` to link the validated account.

tags.name: TrustCore Escrow
tags.description:
TrustCore is PayPetal's **merchant-controlled** escrow product.

**Typical flow:**
1. Create a customer record for both the buyer (initiator) and seller (counterparty).
2. Call `POST /trustcores` to create an agreement — you receive a `paymentUrl`.
3. Redirect the initiator to the payment URL to fund the escrow.
4. PayPetal fires the `trustcore.payment.paid` webhook when the escrow is funded.
5. When the transaction is complete, call `PUT /trustcore/{reference}/complete` to release funds to the counterparty.
6. If the deal falls through, call `PUT /trustcore/{reference}/refund` to return funds to the initiator.

Both complete and refund require the destination customer to have a bank payout account on file.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Exchange your developer credentials for a short-lived JWT Bearer token. All other API endpoints require this token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Tokens are valid for **7 days** — rotate before they expire to avoid service interruption.

tags.name: Bank & Account Tools
tags.description: List supported Nigerian financial institutions and validate a customer's bank account number before linking it as a TrustCore payout destination.

put.description:
Releases the escrowed funds to the merchant. The customer must supply the one-time code received by email after calling `PUT /agreement/auth/{reference}`.

**What happens:**
1. PayPetal validates the authorization code.
2. If valid, the funds are released and the agreement `status` transitions to `COMPLETED`.
3. If the code is invalid or expired, a 400 error is returned — request a new code via `PUT /agreement/auth/{reference}`.

200.description: Funds released successfully. The agreement `status` is now `COMPLETED`. The merchant's account has been credited.

400.description: The code is invalid, expired, or the agreement is not in a completable state. Request a new code via `PUT /agreement/auth/{reference}`.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token.

example.statusResponse: Full authentication is required to access this resource

put.description:
Sends a one-time authorization code to the customer's registered email address.

Call this endpoint when the customer confirms they are ready to release the escrowed funds to the merchant. The customer must then supply that code to `PUT /agreement/complete/{reference}` to complete the release.

**Note:** codes expire after a short window. If the customer does not act in time, call this endpoint again to send a new code.

200.description: Authorization code sent successfully. Instruct the customer to check their email and supply the code to the complete endpoint.

example.message: Authorization code sent to customer email

400.description: Agreement not found, already completed, or not yet funded.

example.message: Agreement not found or is not in a releasable state

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token.

example.statusResponse: Full authentication is required to access this resource

put.description:
Returns the escrowed amount to the **initiator** (the buyer/payer).

**Pre-conditions:**
- The agreement must be in `ONGOING` status.
- The initiator must have a bank payout account on file — add one via `POST /api/v1/escrow/trustcore/payout/{customerId}`.
- `payoutStatus` must be `NONE` — you cannot refund after funds have been released.
- `refundStatus` must be `NONE` — you cannot refund an agreement that has already been refunded.

**What happens next:**
PayPetal debits the TrustCore wallet, sets `refundStatus` to `PENDING`, and queues the bank transfer. The `trustcore.payment.refund` webhook fires when the refund has been processed.

200.description: Refund queued successfully. The `refundStatus` is now `PENDING`. Listen for the `trustcore.payment.refund` webhook to confirm the bank transfer has been processed.

400.description:
The refund cannot proceed. Inspect `responseData.code` for the specific reason.

Common codes: `agreement_not_found`, `payout_completed`, `payout_in_progress`, `already_refunded`, `refund_in_progress`, `missing_payout_account`, `wallet_debit_failed`.

example.message: This agreement has already been refunded.

responseData.message: This agreement has already been refunded.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token.

example.statusResponse: Full authentication is required to access this resource

put.description:
Releases the escrowed amount to the **counterparty** (the seller/receiver).

**Pre-conditions:**
- The agreement must be in `ONGOING` status (i.e., funded by the initiator).
- The counterparty must have a bank payout account on file — add one first via `POST /api/v1/escrow/trustcore/payout/{customerId}`.
- `payoutStatus` must be `NONE` — you cannot release if a payout is already pending, processing, or completed.

**What happens next:**
PayPetal debits the TrustCore wallet, sets `payoutStatus` to `PENDING`, and queues the bank transfer. The `trustcore.payment.completed` webhook fires when the payout is processed.

200.description: Payout queued successfully. The `payoutStatus` is now `PENDING`. Listen for the `trustcore.payment.completed` webhook to confirm the bank transfer has been processed.

400.description:
The release cannot proceed. Inspect `responseData.code` for the specific reason.

Common codes: `agreement_not_found`, `payout_already_completed`, `payout_in_progress`, `missing_payout_account`, `wallet_debit_failed`.

post.description:
Links a validated bank account to a customer as their payout destination for TrustCore releases and refunds.

**Important:** the account number must be pre-validated via `POST /api/v1/account/bank/validate` before calling this endpoint. Always confirm the resolved account name with the customer before saving — PayPetal cannot reverse a payout sent to the wrong account.

post.description:
Creates a pending payment transaction and returns a hosted payment URL. Redirect your customer to `paymentUrl` to complete payment through their PayPetal wallet.

**Idempotency:** supplying a `transactionId` that already exists for a pending transaction returns the existing record instead of creating a new one.

**Rate limit:** 60 requests per 60-second window. Exceeding this returns HTTP 429.

200.description: Payment initiated — redirect the customer to the returned `paymentUrl`.

400.description: Validation error or business profile incomplete.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Parse the retry delay from the response message.

example.message: You have exceeded the allowed number of requests. Try again in 45 second(s).

post.description:
Creates a new customer-controlled escrow agreement and returns a hosted payment URL.

- Set `type` to `ONETIME` for a single payment, or `MILESTONE` for staged releases (requires the `milestone` field).
- `feePayer` controls who bears the PayPetal system fee: `SENDER` adds it to what the customer pays; `RECEIVER` deducts it from the payout.
- Supplying an `idempotencyKey` that already exists returns the original agreement unchanged (idempotent).
- Redirect the customer to `paymentUrl` to fund the escrow.

200.description: Agreement created. Redirect the customer to `responseData.paymentUrl` to fund the escrow. Once funded, the agreement `status` transitions to `FUNDED`.

400.description: Validation failed, the customer was not found, or the idempotency key conflicts with an existing agreement.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token.

example.statusResponse: Full authentication is required to access this resource

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of all TrustCore agreements where the specified customer is either the initiator (payer) or the counterparty (receiver), scoped to the authenticated merchant account.

Results are ordered by creation date, newest first. Use `page` and `size` to iterate through large sets.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: The `customerId` of the customer whose agreements to retrieve.

200.description: Agreements retrieved. `responseData.content` holds the array of agreements. Use `totalPages` and `pageNumber` to build pagination controls in your UI.

400.description: The specified `customerId` does not exist under the authenticated merchant account.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token.

example.statusResponse: Full authentication is required to access this resource

post.description:
Creates a new merchant-controlled escrow agreement between two customers and returns a hosted payment URL.

- The **initiator** is the customer who funds the escrow (the buyer).
- The **counterparty** is the customer who receives the funds on release (the seller).
- Both must exist as customers under your merchant account.
- The `referenceId` must be unique per merchant — reusing an existing reference returns a 400 conflict error.
- Redirect the initiator to `paymentUrl` to complete payment. PayPetal fires the `trustcore.payment.paid` webhook once funded.

200.description: Agreement created successfully. Redirect the initiator to `responseData.paymentUrl` to fund the escrow. The `data` object contains the pending transaction details including the fee breakdown.

400.description:
The request failed validation. Inspect `responseData.type` and `responseData.code` to identify the exact problem.

Common codes: `invalid_amount`, `agreement_exists`, `customer_not_found`, `same_customer`.

example.message: A TrustCore agreement with reference 'ORDER-2024-XYZ-001' already exists.

responseData.message: A TrustCore agreement with reference 'ORDER-2024-XYZ-001' already exists.

post.description:
Exchange Base64-encoded credentials for a JWT Bearer token.

**How to build the credential:**
1. Concatenate your Secret Key and App ID with a colon: `secretKey:appId`
2. Base64-encode the result: `base64('sk_live_abc123:app_xyz789')` → `'c2tfbGl2ZV9hYmMxMjM6YXBwX3h5ejc4OQ=='`
3. Pass the encoded string as `base64Hashed` in the request body.

**Using the token:**
Include the returned `accessToken` in every subsequent request as:
`Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9...`

200.description: Authentication successful. Store the `accessToken` securely — treat it like a password. Check `expireAt` and request a new token before it expires.

400.description: Invalid credentials. Verify that your `secretKey` and `appId` are correct, that the colon separator is present, and that the Base64 encoding has no padding errors.

example.message: Invalid credentials. Please check your secretKey and appId.

status.description: `true` when the operation succeeded; `false` when it failed.

statusCode.description: Application-level result code. `"00"` = success, `"01"` = error. Always inspect the HTTP status code first, then use this field for finer-grained logic.

message.description: Human-readable description of the result. `null` on most successful responses. On error, this contains a plain-English explanation of what went wrong.

dataResponse.description: The response payload. `null` when `status` is `false`. The exact shape varies by endpoint — refer to each endpoint's 200 response example for the structure.

ApiResponse.description:
Standard response envelope returned by all endpoints except TrustCore and TrustVault escrow.

**On success:** `status` is `true`, `statusCode` is `"00"`, and `dataResponse` holds the result.
**On failure:** `status` is `false`, `statusCode` is `"01"`, `message` describes the problem, and `dataResponse` is `null`.

code.description: One-time authorization code sent to the customer's registered email address via PUT /api/v1/escrow/trustvault/agreement/auth/{reference}.

phoneNumber.description: Customer's phone number in international format.

amount.description: Amount in the smallest currency unit (e.g. kobo for NGN, cents for USD).

transactionId.description: Your unique reference for this payment (minimum 14 characters). If omitted, PayPetal generates one. Reusing a reference that belongs to an existing pending transaction returns that transaction instead of creating a new one.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value data stored with the transaction and returned in webhooks and verify calls unchanged.

idempotencyKey.description: Unique key supplied by your platform. Reusing a key returns the original agreement instead of creating a new one (idempotent).

customerId.description: The `customerId` of the customer funding the escrow. Must exist on your merchant account.

amount.description: Amount in the smallest currency unit (e.g. kobo for NGN).

type.description: Agreement type. `ONETIME` for a single payment; `MILESTONE` for staged releases. When `MILESTONE`, the `milestone` field is required.

feePayer.description: Who bears the PayPetal system fee. `SENDER` adds the fee to the amount the customer pays; `RECEIVER` deducts it from the payout.

description.description: Description of the goods or services covered by this agreement.

redirectUrl.description: URL the customer is redirected to after successfully funding the escrow.

additionalProperties.description: Arbitrary key-value data stored with the agreement and returned in responses and webhooks unchanged.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value data stored with the agreement and returned in responses and webhooks unchanged.

amount.description: If amount is not set, then percentage must be set

referenceId.description: A unique reference generated by your platform to identify this escrow transaction. This value must be unique for every transaction and is used for reconciliation and tracking.

initiator.description: The unique identifier of the customer initiating the escrow payment. This customer must exist on your platform.

counterparty.description: The unique identifier of the customer recieving the escrow payment. This customer must exist on your platform.

currency.description: The currency used for the escrow transaction.

amount.description: The escrow amount in the smallest currency unit. For example, NGN should be supplied in kobo.

merchantCharge.description: The additional amount your platform charges your customer as your own commission or service fee. This amount is collected on your behalf and is separate from the PayPetal system fee. Set to 0 or omit this field if you do not want to charge an additional amount.

description.description: A brief description of the goods or services covered by this escrow transaction. This description is visible throughout the transaction lifecycle.
description.example: Payment for iPhone 15 Pro Max, 256GB, Space Black

redirectUrl.description: The URL to which the customer is redirected after successfully funding the escrow. This URL should be handled by your application.

additionalProperties.description: Optional custom data associated with the transaction. TrustCore stores this information and returns it in responses and webhooks without modifying it.

metadata.description: Optional custom data associated with the transaction. TrustCore stores this information and returns it in responses and webhooks without modifying it.

InitiateTrustCoreDto.description: Creates a new TrustCore escrow transaction. TrustCore allows your platform to manage the complete escrow experience while PayPetal securely holds and releases funds. You may optionally specify a merchant charge to earn additional revenue from the transaction. PayPetal system fees are calculated separately based on your merchant fee settings, including who is configured to bear the system fee.

bankCode.description: CBN bank code. Retrieve the full list from GET /api/v1/account/banks.

base64Hashed.description: Base64 encoding of your credentials in the format `secretKey:appId`. Example: `base64('sk_live_abc123:app_xyz789')` → `'c2tfbGl2ZV9hYmMxMjM6YXBwX3h5ejc4OQ=='`

LoginDto.description: Authentication request. Encode your credentials as base64(secretKey:appId) before submitting.

BearerAuth.description: JWT obtained from POST /api/auth/login. Valid for 7 days. Format: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
